title: Lessons in Gun Control From California

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》每日简报 DealBook 的商业与政策记者。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、

sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收听。

sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的萨布丽娜·塔韦尼西。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: In the days after the mass shootings in Buffalo and Uvalde, Texas, Republicans have countered calls for stricter gun laws.
sentences.zh: 在布法罗和得克萨斯州尤瓦尔迪发生大规模枪击事件后的几天里，共和党人反驳了制定更严格枪支法的呼吁。

sentences.en: Restricting the fundamental human right of law-abiding Americans to defend themselves is not the answer.
sentences.zh: 限制守法美国人自卫的基本人权并不是答案。

sentences.en: By saying that there's no evidence that they actually work.
sentences.zh: 通过说没有证据表明它们 실제로 有用。

sentences.en: People who think that, well, maybe we just implement tougher gun laws, it's going to solve it.
sentences.zh: 认为“好吧，也许我们只要实施更严格的枪支法就能解决问题”的人，

sentences.en: Chicago and L.A.
sentences.zh: 芝加哥、洛杉矶

sentences.en: and New York disprove that thesis.
sentences.zh: 和纽约反驳了这一论点。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, Sean Hubler, talks about how one state's experience seems to suggest otherwise.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事肖恩·胡布勒将探讨为什么一个州的经验似乎表明情况并非如此。

sentences.en: Governor Abbott just name-checked the state of California.
sentences.zh: 阿博特州长刚刚点名了加利福尼亚州。

sentences.en: I would caution him from doing that.
sentences.zh: 我要告诫他不要这样做。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, June 2nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月2日，星期四。

sentences.en: So, Sean, gun rights supporters make the case that gun laws don't work.
sentences.zh: 那么，肖恩，枪支权利支持者认为枪支法没有用。

sentences.en: You know, they say that in places where there are lots of gun control laws, there's still lots of mass shootings.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们说在有很多枪支管制法的地方，仍然有许多大规模枪击事件。

sentences.en: So, let's start there.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们从这里开始。

sentences.en: Is that true?
sentences.zh: 这是真的吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Demonstrably true, right?
sentences.zh: 显而易见，对吧？

sentences.en: There are a lot of gun laws, and there are a lot of mass shootings.
sentences.zh: 有很多枪支法律，也有很多大规模枪击事件。

sentences.en: I'm in California.
sentences.zh: 我在加利福尼亚州。

sentences.en: I've been in
sentences.zh: 我一直在

sentences.en: California covering news here for 40 years, and I've covered a lot of the mass shootings here,
sentences.zh: 在加利福尼亚报道这里的新闻已经40年了，我报道过这里的大部分大规模枪击事件，

sentences.en: and there are more in California than there are in any other state in the nation, and California also has some of the toughest gun laws in the nation.
sentences.zh: 加州的大规模枪击事件比全国任何其他州都多，而且加州也拥有全国最严格的一些枪支法律。

sentences.en: So, yes, those folks are right.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，那些人是对的。

sentences.en: It is true that there are a lot of mass shootings, even though there are a lot of gun laws.
sentences.zh: 尽管有很多枪支法律，但确实有很多大规模枪击事件，这是事实。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: But it's also wrong to say that gun laws don't prevent mass shootings.
sentences.zh: 但说枪支法律不能阻止大规模枪击事件也是错误的。

sentences.en: The way to look at it is more along the lines of proportion to the population.
sentences.zh: 看待这个问题的方式更应该从占人口比例的角度出发。

sentences.en: California has nearly 40 million people.
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚州有近4000万人口。

sentences.en: It has more people than any other state in the nation.
sentences.zh: 它的人口比全国任何其他州都多。

sentences.en: It would be strange if it didn't have a lot of mass shootings compared to other states.
sentences.zh: 与其他州相比，如果没有很多大规模枪击事件，那才奇怪呢。

sentences.en: It's got more people than other states.
sentences.zh: 它的人口比其他州多。

sentences.en: But if you look at it the way that researchers, gun violence researchers, look at it on a basis of how many people get killed by guns per 100,000 population.
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你按照研究人员、枪支暴力研究人员的方式来看待它，即每 10 万人口中有多少人死于枪支。

sentences.en: As a proportion of the population?
sentences.zh: 按人口比例算？

sentences.en: As a proportion of the population.
sentences.zh: 按人口比例算。

sentences.en: By that measure, California's gun violence rates are really, really low.
sentences.zh: 通过这个标准，加利福尼亚州的枪支暴力率确实非常非常低。

sentences.en: They're among the lowest in the country.
sentences.zh: 它们是全国最低的之一。

sentences.en: Okay, so tell me about that.
sentences.zh: 好的，跟我讲讲这个。

sentences.en: California has about eight and a half gun deaths per 100,000 people.
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚州每 10 万人中约有 8.5 起枪支死亡事件。

sentences.en: That was in 2020.
sentences.zh: 那是 2020 年的数据。

sentences.en: It's the most recent year for which statistics are available.
sentences.zh: 这是有统计数据的最近一年。

sentences.en: By comparison, there were about 13.7 gun deaths nationally per 100,000 people.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，全国范围内每 10 万人中约有 13.7 起枪支死亡事件。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: So you're about 40% less likely to die of firearm violence in California than you are in the rest of the country.
sentences.zh: 因此，在加利福尼亚州死于枪支暴力的可能性比在全国其他地方低约 40%。

sentences.en: So, Sean, how did California get that way?
sentences.zh: 那么，肖恩，加州是怎么变成这样的？

sentences.en: Well, there are a lot of factors, of course, when it comes to gun violence, poverty, joblessness,
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然有很多因素，当谈到枪支暴力时，贫困、失业，

sentences.en: demographics.
sentences.zh: 人口统计。

sentences.en: But one of the main drivers of California's low gun death rates are actually gun laws.
sentences.zh: 但加州枪支死亡率低的主要驱动因素之一实际上是枪支法律。

sentences.en: So let's go back to the beginning.
sentences.zh: 让我们回到最初。

sentences.en: What did California do?
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚做了什么？

sentences.en: California tends to get to places a little sooner than the rest of the country.
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚往往比全国其他地方更早到达一些地方。

sentences.en: And California had one of the earliest, most influential gun control laws back in the 60s.
sentences.zh: 加州在 60 年代制定了最早、最具影响力的枪支管制法之一。

sentences.en: In the 60s, in the Bay Area, the Black activist group, the Black Panthers, was doing armed patrols in Oakland.
sentences.zh: 在 60 年代的湾区，黑人激进组织“黑豹党”正在奥克兰进行武装巡逻。

sentences.en: The police in our community couldn't possibly be there to protect our property because we own no property.
sentences.zh: 我们社区的警察根本不可能在那里保护我们的财产，因为我们没有财产。

sentences.en: They were doing something they called cop watching.
sentences.zh: 他们在做他们称之为警察监视的事情。

sentences.en: They were concerned about racial justice and police brutality.
sentences.zh: 他们关心的是种族正义和警察暴力。

sentences.en: And the police were there not to promote our welfare or for our security and our safety.
sentences.zh: 警察的存在不是为了促进我们的福利或我们的安全和保障。

sentences.en: And they were keeping their own eyes on the problem.
sentences.zh: 他们自己也在密切关注这个问题。

sentences.en: They were patrolling their own neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 他们在自己的社区巡逻。

sentences.en: But they're there to contain us, to brutalize us and murder us.
sentences.zh: 但他们的存在是为了遏制我们、对我们施暴并谋杀我们。

sentences.en: And the legislature in Sacramento was nervous and wanted to put a stop to that.
sentences.zh: 萨克拉门托的立法机关很紧张，想要制止这种行为。

sentences.en: You have to keep in mind, these lawmakers were mostly white.
sentences.zh: 你必须记住，这些立法者大多是白人。

sentences.en: They were having a reaction to Black people carrying around loaded guns, doing their own patrols of their own neighborhoods in an area
sentences.zh: 他们对黑人随身携带装有子弹的枪支、在某个地区对自己的社区进行自己的巡逻做出了反应

sentences.en: where the police at the time also were mostly white.
sentences.zh: 当时的警察也大多是白人。

sentences.en: And so the state legislature decides to look at a law to restrict open carrying in public, which is what the Black Panthers were doing.
sentences.zh: 因此，州立法机关决定研究一项法律，以限制在公共场合公开携带枪支，黑豹党当时就是这么做的。

sentences.en: So on the day of the debate...
sentences.zh: 所以在辩论的那天……

sentences.en: Am I under arrest?
sentences.zh: 我被捕了吗？

sentences.en: Am I under arrest?
sentences.zh: 我被捕了吗？

sentences.en: Am I under arrest?
sentences.zh: 我被捕了吗？

sentences.en: You place them under arreSt. Go ahead.
sentences.zh: 你把他们逮捕了。继续。

sentences.en: Take your hands off me if I'm not under arreSt.
sentences.zh: 如果我没有被捕，把你的手拿开。

sentences.en: The Black Panthers showed up to the state capitol for the hearing, and they were carrying guns to show that this was their right to do this.
sentences.zh: 黑豹党出现在州议会大厦参加听证会，他们带着枪以表明这是他们这样做的权利。

sentences.en: The Black Panther Party for Self-Defense calls upon the American people in general, and the Black people in particular, take full note of the racist California legislature,
sentences.zh: 自卫黑豹党呼吁广大美国人民，特别是黑人人民，充分注意种族主义的加利福尼亚州立法机关，

sentences.en: which is now considering legislation aimed at keeping the Black people disarmed and powerless
sentences.zh: 该机构目前正在审议旨在解除黑人武装并剥夺其权力的立法

sentences.en: at the very same time that racist police agencies throughout the country are intensifying the terror, brutality, murder, and repression of Black people.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，全国各地的种族主义警察机构正在加剧对黑人的恐怖、残酷、谋杀和镇压。

sentences.en: And in fairly short order, this mostly white legislature voted to pass this gun control law that restricted open carrying.
sentences.zh: 在很短的时间内，这个大多是白人的立法机关投票通过了这项限制公开携带枪支的枪支管制法。

sentences.en: And the governor, who at the time was Ronald Reagan, signed the bill into law.
sentences.zh: 当时的州长罗纳德·里根签署了该法案使其成为法律。

sentences.en: There is absolutely no reason why out on the street today civilians should be carrying a loaded weapon.
sentences.zh: 今天在街上，平民绝对没有任何理由携带装有子弹的武器。

sentences.en: So it sounds like racial fears and racism was a major motivator for one of California's early efforts at gun control.
sentences.zh: 听起来种族恐惧和种族主义是加州早期枪支管制努力的主要推动力。

sentences.en: You could argue that.
sentences.zh: 你可以这么争辩。

sentences.en: This was the 60s, and it prompted a wave of federal legislation at the time, and it also kind of prompted a wave of interest by gun owners in making sure that their rights were not
sentences.zh: 那是 60 年代，它引发了一波联邦立法浪潮，它也某种程度上引发了枪支所有者确保他们的权利不受侵犯的兴趣

sentences.en: impaired to carry guns.
sentences.zh: 携带枪支受损。

sentences.en: So in some respects, this was kind of the beginning of the modern gun debate.
sentences.zh: 因此，在某些方面，这可以说是现代枪支辩论的开始。

sentences.en: So, Sean, what happened next?
sentences.zh: 那么，肖恩，接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, over time, California passed waves of gun legislation.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，加州通过了一波又一波的枪支立法。

sentences.en: It's usually prompted, as it is in a lot of places, by some big event, some big scary issue.
sentences.zh: 它通常是由某个重大事件、某个重大可怕的问题引发的，就像在许多地方一样。

sentences.en: At Cleveland Elementary today, school began on time, but not as usual.
sentences.zh: 今天在克利夫兰小学，学校准时上课，但并不像平常一样。

sentences.en: So in the late 1980s, in 1989, there was a shooting at a schoolyard in Stockton.
sentences.zh: 所以在 20 世纪 80 年代末，即 1989 年，斯托克顿发生了一起学校操场枪击事件。

sentences.en: Witnesses say a lone gunman walked onto the campus at Stockton's Cleveland Elementary School and opened fire with a machine gun.
sentences.zh: 目击者称，一名枪手独自走进斯托克顿克利夫兰小学的校园，用机枪开枪。

sentences.en: At the time, four to five hundred first, second, and third graders were playing during their lunch period.
sentences.zh: 当时，四五百名一、二、三年级学生正在午休期间玩耍。

sentences.en: A guy walked into a schoolyard with an AK-47.
sentences.zh: 一个人拿着 AK-47 走进了学校操场。

sentences.en: When the rampage was over, five students lay dead.
sentences.zh: 当暴行结束时，五名学生倒地身亡。

sentences.en: A teacher and more than 30 students were injured, more than half of them critically.
sentences.zh: 一名教师和 30 多名学生受伤，其中一半以上伤势严重。

sentences.en: At the time, the state legislature acted again.
sentences.zh: 当时，州议会再次采取行动。

sentences.en: This time, they banned assault weapons.
sentences.zh: 这一次，他们禁止了突击武器。

sentences.en: And that was a pivotal action on the part of California.
sentences.zh: 这是加利福尼亚方面采取的关键行动。

sentences.en: With that law came a bunch of other laws.
sentences.zh: 随着这项法律的出台，还出台了一系列其他法律。

sentences.en: The state banned private gun sales.
sentences.zh: 该州禁止私人枪支销售。

sentences.en: It made sure that gun sales had to be through dealers, who in turn had to be licensed.
sentences.zh: 它确保枪支销售必须通过经销商进行，而经销商反过来必须获得许可。

sentences.en: The state started to require background checks.
sentences.zh: 该州开始要求进行背景调查。

sentences.en: And people who were convicted of violent crimes, and this is key, violent misdemeanors, like assault and battery, were going to be prohibited from buying guns.
sentences.zh: 因暴力犯罪被定罪的人，关键是暴力轻罪，如殴打和攻击，将被禁止购买枪支。

sentences.en: And then...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: Darkness descends on Los Angeles, and the gangs and their guns hit the streets again.
sentences.zh: 夜幕降临洛杉矶，帮派和他们的枪支再次走上街头。

sentences.en: There was a wave of gang crime in California.
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚州爆发了一波帮派犯罪浪潮。

sentences.en: Shot in the leg, a gang member runs for his life.
sentences.zh: 腿部中弹，一名帮派成员夺路而逃。

sentences.en: It was an epidemic.
sentences.zh: 这是一场流行病。

sentences.en: Everyone is saying that this problem is getting out of hand, and they're trying to do something about it.
sentences.zh: 每个人都说这个问题已经失控了，他们正试图采取行动。

sentences.en: It was a terrible problem, and it was fueled in part by the availability of cheap handguns.
sentences.zh: 这是一个可怕的问题，部分原因是廉价手枪的泛滥。

sentences.en: Saturday night specials, you've heard the phrase.
sentences.zh: 周六夜特价枪，你听过这个短语。

sentences.en: But define it for me.
sentences.zh: 但请为我定义一下。

sentences.en: They were cheap handguns.
sentences.zh: 它们是廉价手枪。

sentences.en: They were cheap, easy to use, easily accessible.
sentences.zh: 它们便宜、易于使用、易于获得。

sentences.en: But they didn't always function the way that they were supposed to.
sentences.zh: 但它们的运作并不总是如预期那样。

sentences.en: They broke easily, and the state decided to go after them in a way that was innovative at the time.
sentences.zh: 它们很容易坏，州政府决定以当时创新的方式对付它们。

sentences.en: They went after it by imposing consumer product legislation.
sentences.zh: 他们通过实施消费品立法来解决这个问题。

sentences.en: They said, okay, if you're going to manufacture cheap handguns, fine, but they have to meet certain specifications.
sentences.zh: 他们说，好吧，如果你要制造廉价手枪，没问题，但它们必须符合特定的规格。

sentences.en: And here's what these specifications are.
sentences.zh: 这些规格如下。

sentences.en: And they sort of went after them using consumer product law.
sentences.zh: 他们有点像利用消费品法来对付他们。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: Yeah, it made a big difference.
sentences.zh: 是的，这产生了很大的影响。

sentences.en: Much of the Saturday night special market was in and around Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 周六夜特价枪市场的大部分都在洛杉矶及其周边地区。

sentences.en: The manufacturers were only a handful of companies, and they were mostly around L.A.
sentences.zh: 制造商只有几家公司，而且大多在洛杉矶附近

sentences.en: And within a fairly short period of time, most of the manufacturers had either moved to Nevada or gone out of business.
sentences.zh: 在相当短的时间内，大多数制造商要么搬到了内华达州，要么倒闭了。

sentences.en: And they weren't replaced on the market, and it was very expensive to meet these specifications.
sentences.zh: 而且市场上没有替代品，而且满足这些规格的成本非常高。

sentences.en: So, Sean, what was the effect of these laws?
sentences.zh: 那么，肖恩，这些法律的效果是什么？

sentences.en: I mean, the measurable effect that they had on gun mortality, on gun deaths.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们对枪支死亡率、枪支死亡人数产生的可衡量影响。

sentences.en: So, each of these new laws took time to refine and to come online.
sentences.zh: 因此，每项新法律都需要时间来完善并上线。

sentences.en: And so, you don't see the effect immediately.
sentences.zh: 所以，你不会立即看到效果。

sentences.en: And you don't see one single law having a dramatic effect.
sentences.zh: 你也不会看到单一法律产生巨大影响。

sentences.en: But in 1999, California had roughly nine deaths by firearm for every 100,000 people.
sentences.zh: 但在 1999 年，加利福尼亚州每 10 万人中大约有 9 人死于枪支。

sentences.en: And the rest of the country had roughly 10 deaths per 100,000 population.
sentences.zh: 全国其他地区每 10 万人口大约有 10 人死亡。

sentences.en: It was fairly close.
sentences.zh: 这非常接近。

sentences.en: You were about as likely to be killed by a gun in California as you were in the rest of the country in 1999.
sentences.zh: 在 1999 年，你在加利福尼亚州被枪杀的可能性与在全国其他地方差不多。

sentences.en: But over the next 20 years or so, bit by bit, law by law, refinement by refinement, the number of gun deaths begin in California to slope downward.
sentences.zh: 但在接下来的 20 年左右里，一点一点地，法律接法律，改进接改进，加利福尼亚州的枪支死亡人数开始呈下降趋势。

sentences.en: You can trace the line.
sentences.zh: 你可以追溯这条线。

sentences.en: So that by 2019, California's gun deaths had fallen from nine per 100,000 to about seven per 100,000.
sentences.zh: 因此，到 2019 年，加利福尼亚州的枪支死亡人数已从每 10 万人 9 人下降到每 10 万人 7 人左右。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, they had gone up in the rest of the country.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，全国其他地区的数字却在上升。

sentences.en: So there was a huge differential by 2019, before the pandemic started.
sentences.zh: 因此，到 2019 年大流行开始之前，存在着巨大的差距。

sentences.en: The chances of dying from gun violence in California were about 50 percent lower than they were in the rest of the country, even though it's an enormous state.
sentences.zh: 在加利福尼亚州死于枪支暴力的几率比全国其他地区低约 50%，尽管它是一个巨大的州。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 首次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在该应用内的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是《纽约时报》的订阅者，今天就下载《时报》应用，即可免费使用30天。

sentences.en: So, Sean, from what you're saying, it really does seem like each one of these interventions, these gun restrictions, has led to a meaningful decrease in gun deaths.
sentences.zh: 那么，肖恩，根据你的说法，这些干预措施中的每一项、这些枪支限制措施，似乎确实都大幅减少了涉枪死亡人数。

sentences.en: But my question for you is, how do we know that it was the laws themselves that caused it?
sentences.zh: 但我的问题是，我们怎么知道是这些法律本身导致了这种结果？

sentences.en: I mean, as you said earlier, there are lots of factors that contribute to gun violence.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如你刚才所说，导致枪支暴力的因素有很多。

sentences.en: Well, California is one of the few states that does its own gun violence research.
sentences.zh: 加州是少数几个开展自己的枪支暴力研究的州之一。

sentences.en: And they research the efficacy of these policies that they passed to see kind of what works, what doesn't work, how it works.
sentences.zh: 他们研究自己通过的这些政策的有效性，来看看哪种有用、哪种没用、以及它是如何起作用的。

sentences.en: And so, for example, someone who's done a lot of work on gun violence in California, a researcher, a physician named Garen Wintemute, who's at the University of California, Davis.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，加州有一位长期从事枪支暴力研究的学者，是一位名叫加伦·温特穆特（Garen Wintemute）的研究员、医师，他在加州大学戴维斯分校工作。

sentences.en: He looked at things like the effect of the law that prohibits people here who are convicted of violent misdemeanors from having guns.
sentences.zh: 他研究了诸如禁止被判犯有暴力轻罪的人拥有枪支的法律的效果。

sentences.en: Most states will have a law that says you can't own a gun if you're convicted of a felony.
sentences.zh: 大多数州都会有法律规定，如果被判犯有重罪，你就不能拥有枪支。

sentences.en: But California has a law that says it's not just a felony that will bar you from having a gun.
sentences.zh: 但加州的法律规定，不仅是重罪会剥夺你拥有枪支的资格。

sentences.en: It's a violent misdemeanor, too, assault and battery.
sentences.zh: 暴力轻罪也是如此，比如袭击和殴打罪。

sentences.en: That law is one of the older ones.
sentences.zh: 那项法律是比较早的法律之一。

sentences.en: It was passed in, like, 1990.
sentences.zh: 它大约是在1990年左右通过的。

sentences.en: They took a look at people who were convicted of violent misdemeanors the year before that law went into effect and the year after that law went into effect.
sentences.zh: 他们调查了在该法律生效前一年以及生效后一年因暴力轻罪而被定罪的人。

sentences.en: And they tracked those people for three years to see whether people who had been denied guns were more or less likely to commit another violent crime.
sentences.zh: 他们对这些人进行了三年的追踪调查，以观察被剥夺购枪权的人再次犯下暴力犯罪的可能性是更高还是更低。

sentences.en: Turns out denying them guns reduced the rate of violent crime.
sentences.zh: 结果证明，剥夺他们拥有枪支的权利减少了暴力犯罪率。

sentences.en: They were 25 to 30 percent less likely to be charged with a new violent crime.
sentences.zh: 他们被指控犯下新暴力犯罪的可能性降低了25%到30%。

sentences.en: Researchers in California have also looked at things like gun violence restraining orders.
sentences.zh: 加州的研究人员还研究了诸如枪支暴力限制令之类的事情。

sentences.en: You might know them as red flag laws.
sentences.zh: 你可能知道它们被称为红旗法案。

sentences.en: Those are laws that allow the authorities to remove guns from people proactively if they're deemed to be a danger to themselves or others.
sentences.zh: 这些法律允许当局在认定某人对自身或他人构成危险时，主动收缴其枪支。

sentences.en: And almost immediately after that law was passed, the research began.
sentences.zh: 在该法律通过后几乎立刻，相关研究就开始了。

sentences.en: And California looked at, for example, the first sort of batch of restraining orders that were issued in the first couple of years.
sentences.zh: 加州研究了例如头两年发布的第一批限制令。

sentences.en: And they looked at those, they found that out of that batch, about a third of them had been issued because of concerns about mass shootings.
sentences.zh: 他们对这些限制令进行了研究，发现其中大约有三分之一是因为担心大规模枪击事件而发布的。

sentences.en: The person had made a kind of a credible threat of a mass shooting, and people were worried about that.
sentences.zh: 当事人曾发出过某种可信的大规模枪击威胁，人们对此感到担忧。

sentences.en: Of course, there's no way to know, you know, what would have happened had the order not been issued, right, had the guns not been taken away.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果没有发布限制令、没有收缴枪支，事情会变成怎样，我们是无从得知的，对吧？

sentences.en: But what they did find was that, okay, did any of these people then find another way to commit a mass shooting, even though we took the guns away from them?
sentences.zh: 但他们发现的是，好吧，这些人后来有没有找到其他方式来实施大规模枪击，尽管我们收缴了他们的枪支？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They did not.
sentences.zh: 他们没有。

sentences.en: Zero of them had found a workaround to commit a mass shooting, even though they had threatened one and their guns were taken away.
sentences.zh: 他们当中没有一个人找到变通办法来实施大规模枪击，尽管他们曾发出过威胁且枪支已被收缴。

sentences.en: So the state does know that, you know, there's no perfect way to know for sure because you're proving a negative, right?
sentences.zh: 所以该州确实知道，你知道，没有完美的办法去百分之百确定，因为你是在证明一个否定命题，对吧？

sentences.en: You're proving the crime that didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 你是在证明那个没有发生的犯罪。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But there are ways to go back and design studies to get a fairly specific sense of whether these rules and new laws and policies work in California.
sentences.zh: 但有办法回过头来设计研究，从而获得一个相当明确的概念，弄清楚这些规则、新法律和政策在加州是否奏效。

sentences.en: And one of the things that they're looking at is not just which specific laws work in which specific way, but how do the laws work as a bundle in concert?
sentences.zh: 他们正在研究的事情之一，不仅是哪些具体的法律以哪些具体的方式起作用，还有这些法律作为一个组合如何共同发挥作用？

sentences.en: How do the laws work together?
sentences.zh: 这些法律是如何协同作用的？

sentences.en: And that seems to be a key question because the effect of these laws is not just one at a time in some dramatic way.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是一个关键问题，因为这些法律的效果并非仅仅孤立地以某种戏剧性的方式展现。

sentences.en: The effect of these laws is cumulative as a package.
sentences.zh: 这些法律的效果是作为一个整体累积产生的。

sentences.en: It reminds me personally of the approach that public health policymakers have made around the country to COVID.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起了全国各地的公共卫生决策者对新冠疫情采取的方法。

sentences.en: They call it the Swiss cheese approach in which you layer a lot of policies on top of each other so that even though there are holes in the policies, the holes don't line up.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为瑞士奶酪模型，即将许多政策层层叠加，这样一来，即使政策中存在漏洞，这些漏洞也不会重合。

sentences.en: In the same way that we limit our risk of COVID by getting vaccinated and wearing masks and doing testing, in that same way, California has layered gun laws.
sentences.zh: 就像我们通过接种疫苗、佩戴口罩和进行检测来降低感染新冠的风险一样，加州也同样层层叠加了枪支法律。

sentences.en: California has kind of gone after this particular public health risk in the same way that we go after other public health risks in the rest of the country.
sentences.zh: 加州应对这种特定的公共卫生风险的方式，与我们全国其他地方应对其他公共卫生风险的方式如出一辙。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So California is essentially measuring itself, right?
sentences.zh: 所以加州基本上是在衡量自身，对吧？

sentences.en: These laws it's passed.
sentences.zh: 也就是它通过的这些法律。

sentences.en: And it sounds like what it's finding is that when it looks at the before and after on a whole bunch of different gun laws, not just one.
sentences.zh: 听起来它的发现是，当它考察一大堆不同的枪支法律的前后对比时，而不仅仅是一项法律。

sentences.en: They can tell that there is an effect.
sentences.zh: 他们能看出确实产生了效果。

sentences.en: And even more than that, they can tell that these laws, when taken all together, the sum total of them, when, as you say, layered on like pieces of Swiss cheese, slice after slice,
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，他们还能看出，当把这些法律全部综合起来，将其总效果（正如你所说）像瑞士奶酪的片片切片那样层层叠加时，

sentences.en: the holes are covered up and the impact is really meaningful.
sentences.zh: 漏洞就被覆盖了，产生的影响确实意义重大。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: You know, here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，情况是这样的。

sentences.en: Californians aren't that different from the rest of America.
sentences.zh: 加州人跟美国其他地区的人并没有太大区别。

sentences.en: America, they lose their temper, they have mental breakdowns, they commit crimes, there are social stresses.
sentences.zh: 在美国，人们会发脾气、会精神崩溃、会犯罪、存在社会压力。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: All of the same factors that feed gun violence in the rest of the country exist in California.
sentences.zh: 助长全国其他地区枪支暴力的所有相同因素在加州也都存在。

sentences.en: The one thing that is different is the policy.
sentences.zh: 唯一不同的地方在于政策。

sentences.en: Now, there is one exception.
sentences.zh: 不过，有一个例外。

sentences.en: The pandemic has bumped gun violence up across the country, in California as well.
sentences.zh: 大流行推高了全国各地的枪支暴力，加州也是如此。

sentences.en: Murders and suicides, which is a huge part, by the way, of gun statistics.
sentences.zh: 谋杀和自杀，顺便说一句，这是枪支统计数据中极大的一个部分。

sentences.en: I mean, suicides are a big part of gun deaths in this country and in California as well.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，自杀占了这个国家以及加州枪支死亡人数的很大一部分。

sentences.en: Two-thirds, I believe, right?
sentences.zh: 我想是三分之二，对吧？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So across the country and in California, well, California has not been immune.
sentences.zh: 所以在全国各地以及加州，好吧，加州也未能幸免。

sentences.en: But again, have they bumped up anywhere close to meeting the rest of the country?
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，它们的飙升幅度接近全国其他地方吗？

sentences.en: No, they have not.
sentences.zh: 没有，并没有。

sentences.en: The differential is still enormous.
sentences.zh: 这种差距依然巨大。

sentences.en: You're still way, way less likely to die of a gunshot in California than you are in the rest of the United States.
sentences.zh: 在加州，你因枪击身亡的可能性仍然远远低于美国其他地区。

sentences.en: So by process of elimination, in a sense, these policies are working.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，通过排除法，这些政策正在起作用。

sentences.en: So, Sean, what about people who will always find a way, you know, even if they aren't allowed to buy a gun?
sentences.zh: 那么，肖恩，那些无论如何总能找到办法的人又该怎么说呢，你知道的，即使他们不被允许买枪？

sentences.en: Say, you know, someone who has a criminal record who's really determined to get one.
sentences.zh: 比如说，你知道的，某个有犯罪前科、一心想要弄到一把枪的人。

sentences.en: I mean, there's this common argument that laws don't matter because people will always find a way around them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有一种常见的论点认为法律无关紧要，因为人们总能找到绕过法律的办法。

sentences.en: So are laws meaningful when we know people don't follow them?
sentences.zh: 那么，既然我们知道人们不遵守法律，法律还有意义吗？

sentences.en: So, you know, yeah, there will always be people who break the law, you know, and it's not like California's experience is everyone's experience.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，是的，总会有人触犯法律，而且加州的经验也并非所有人的经验。

sentences.en: Illinois, for example, has strict gun laws as well.
sentences.zh: 例如，伊利诺伊州也有严格的枪支法律。

sentences.en: And their rate of death by firearm is higher than California's.
sentences.zh: 但他们因枪支致死的比率比加州还要高。

sentences.en: It's comparable to Texas's, in fact.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它与得克萨斯州不相上下。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 真有趣。

sentences.en: There are a lot of reasons for that, complicated reasons for that.
sentences.zh: 造成这种情况的原因有很多，原因很复杂。

sentences.en: For one thing, they're surrounded by places with much more permissive gun laws,
sentences.zh: 一方面，他们被枪支法律更为宽松的地方所包围，

sentences.en: and they have a much harder time preventing guns from other states from finding their way into Chicago, where people use them to commit crimes.
sentences.zh: 而且他们很难阻止来自其他州的枪支流入芝加哥，人们在那里用这些枪支犯罪。

sentences.en: But each place is always going to have its own sort of specific local landscape that has to be dealt with.
sentences.zh: 但每个地方总会有其自身需要应对的特定地方局势。

sentences.en: But the way I think about it is more in terms of the way the world actually works as opposed to the way the world works in theory.
sentences.zh: 不过我考虑问题的方式，更多是从世界实际运转的方式出发，而不是从世界在理论上运转的方式出发。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of people think it's all or nothing, on or off, good or bad, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，很多人认为一切非黑即白，非开即关，非好即坏，对吧？

sentences.en: But the way that the world actually works is more in terms of better and worse, more or less.
sentences.zh: 但世界实际运转的方式更多体现在更好与更坏、更多与更少上。

sentences.en: You know, something that was really interesting that the doctor went to mute, the researcher here in California, said to me the other day when I interviewed him.
sentences.zh: 你知道，加州的研究人员温特穆特医生前几天我采访他时说的一件事非常有意思。

sentences.en: He said, people will say there are all sorts of laws in California, and they're still not working.
sentences.zh: 他说，人们会说加州有各种各样的法律，但它们还是不管用。

sentences.en: There was just a mass shooting here, you know, a couple of weeks ago in California.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就在几周前加州刚发生了一起大规模枪击事件。

sentences.en: Obviously, these laws aren't working.
sentences.zh: 很明显，这些法律根本不管用。

sentences.en: But you wouldn't say that a law that was lowering your risk of gun death compared to the rest of the country,
sentences.zh: 但你不会因为一项法律未能将你的枪支死亡风险降低100%（与全国其他地区相比），

sentences.en: you wouldn't say that that law was a failure just because it wasn't 100%.
sentences.zh: 就不会说那项法律是失败的。

sentences.en: You would say, wow, I'm a lot safer in California.
sentences.zh: 你会说，哇，我在加州安全多了。

sentences.en: You know, so an approach that reduces gun deaths, it's not a failure because it doesn't reduce those gun deaths by 100%.
sentences.zh: 所以，一种减少枪支死亡的方略，并不会因为它没有把枪支死亡人数减少100%而成为失败之举。

sentences.en: That being said, limiting gun deaths is an ongoing project in California, you know, and sometimes there are unintended consequences.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，在加州限制枪支死亡是一个持续进行的项目，你知道的，有时也会产生意想不到的后果。

sentences.en: For example, the fact that California has limited gun availability in the state, that has created in California, ironically, a market for ghost guns,
sentences.zh: 例如，加州限制了州内枪支的获得这一事实，具有讽刺意味的是，在加州催生了一个幽灵枪市场，

sentences.en: which have become a real problem.
sentences.zh: 这已经成了一个真正的问题。

sentences.en: These are guns that are unregistered, they're sold often in kits, they don't have a serial number on them, you can't trace them, you can buy them often online.
sentences.zh: 这些枪支未曾登记，通常以套件形式出售，上面没有序列号，你无法追踪它们，而且你通常可以在网上买到。

sentences.en: They're a real concern in California.
sentences.zh: 它们在加州引起了切实的担忧。

sentences.en: And it would seem like those guns exist in a lot of ways in the state of California because other legal guns are harder to get, right?
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，这些枪支之所以存在于加州，似乎是因为其他合法的枪支更难买到了，对吧？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They fill a niche in the market, an opening in the market, there's a demand for them, right?
sentences.zh: 它们填补了市场上的一个空白，市场上有这种需求，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But the way that the state has come to view it is, okay, well, we just need another layer of Swiss cheese then.
sentences.zh: 但该州现在的看法是，好吧，那我们只需要再加一层瑞士奶酪就行了。

sentences.en: Let's take a look at these ghost guns and we'll try to do something about that.
sentences.zh: 让我们来看看这些幽灵枪，然后试着采取点措施。

sentences.en: And so the state, in fact, right now, is considering legislation to address ghost guns and other holes.
sentences.zh: 事实上，该州目前正在审议旨在解决幽灵枪及其他漏洞的立法。

sentences.en: And so, for example, right now, the state legislature is looking at a law that would do for banned illegal guns in California what Texas did to restrict abortion.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，目前州议会正在审议一项法律，该法律对加州被禁的非法枪支所起的作用，就像得州限制堕胎的法律一样。

sentences.en: Oh, really?
sentences.zh: 哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: So tell me how that would work.
sentences.zh: 那请告诉我这会是如何运作的。

sentences.en: Well, so remember a few months ago, Texas put into place a law that encourages private citizens to sue anyone who, quote, aids and abets an abortion.
sentences.zh: 好的，还记得几个月前，得州实施了一项法律，鼓励普通公民起诉任何，引用原话，“协助和教唆堕胎”的人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Well, California is working on a law that is modeled on that.
sentences.zh: 加州目前正在制订一项以该法为蓝本的法律。

sentences.en: It's fast-tracking it, in fact, and we expect it to be passed fairly soon.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它正在加快推进，我们预计它很快就会通过。

sentences.en: And that law offers financial incentives for people to file civil lawsuits against anybody who sells or manufactures guns that California has outlawed, including ghost guns.
sentences.zh: 该法律为对任何出售或制造加州已取缔的枪支（包括幽灵枪）的人提起民事诉讼的个人提供经济奖励。

sentences.en: So I'm remembering, Sean, that the Texas law, of course, was a law that essentially deputized ordinary people to go out and sue abortion providers, Uber drivers,
sentences.zh: 肖恩，我记得得州的法律当然是一项基本上授权普通民众去起诉堕胎提供者、优步司机、

sentences.en: anybody who was involved in abortion in the state.
sentences.zh: 以及任何在州内参与堕胎的人的法律。

sentences.en: So it was a really radical approach legally, right?
sentences.zh: 所以在法律上这是一种非常激进的做法，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it was essentially stripping away somebody's federally protected constitutional right at the state level.
sentences.zh: 因为它本质上是在州层面剥夺了某人受联邦保护的宪法权利。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: At the state level by using the civil courts.
sentences.zh: 在州层面通过利用民事法庭来做到这一点。

sentences.en: And in fact, the governor here, California is a heavily democratic state, and the governor here had spoken against the Texas law and thought that it was a bad idea.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这里的州长——加州是一个民主党势力强大的州——这里的州长曾公开反对得州的法律，认为这是一个馊主意。

sentences.en: But when the Supreme Court more or less upheld what Texas was doing, that particular tactic, California said, fine, what's good for one is good for the other.
sentences.zh: 但当最高法院大致维持了得州的做法时，加州针对那种特定的策略表示：好吧，适用于一方的也适用于另一方。

sentences.en: And we're going to do for guns what you've done for abortion.
sentences.zh: 我们要对枪支采取你们对堕胎采取的手段。

sentences.en: It's a similar strategy.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相似的策略。

sentences.en: It's we're not going to just go directly at the problem.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们不直接针对问题正面出击。

sentences.en: We're going to chip away at it bit by bit in the same way that Texas has passed for many decades laws that chipped away at the availability of abortion.
sentences.zh: 我们要一点一点地削弱它，就像得州几十年来通过法律逐步削弱堕胎的可及性一样。

sentences.en: In the same way Texas has done that, California has done the same thing with guns.
sentences.zh: 正如得州所做的那样，加州对枪支也采取了同样的做法。

sentences.en: And advocates in both states would argue that they've saved lives.
sentences.zh: 两州的倡导者都会辩称他们挽救了生命。

sentences.en: So it's in a sense, it kind of makes sense that if Texas says, OK, we can't ban all abortions,
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，这挺合乎逻辑的：如果得州说，好吧，我们不能禁止所有堕胎，

sentences.en: but we're going to sue you so much and so often that you're not going to want to bother with this.
sentences.zh: 但我们要频繁地起诉你，告到你觉得不值得为此费劲。

sentences.en: In the same way, California is now going to try that approach as well.
sentences.zh: 同理，加州现在也要尝试这种方法。

sentences.en: We can't maybe stop the flow of of ghost guns into the state ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们或许无法亲自阻止幽灵枪流入本州。

sentences.en: But the threat of lawsuit is going to hang so heavily over these ghost gun manufacturers and the salespeople of these kits and so on that they're not going to want to bother.
sentences.zh: 但诉讼的威胁将沉重地悬在这些幽灵枪制造商、这些套件的销售人员等等的头上，以至于他们觉得不值得去费这个劲。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I guess I'm reminded, Sean, of a lot of years I've done reporting on abortion legislation in this country.
sentences.zh: 我想我记起了，肖恩，我报道这个国家的堕胎立法已经很多年了。

sentences.en: And, you know, as you say, the strategy has been chipping away at this constitutional right.
sentences.zh: 你知道，正如你所说，这一直以来的策略就是逐步侵蚀这项宪法权利。

sentences.en: You know, each individual law might not amount to much,
sentences.zh: 你知道，每一项单独的法律可能算不上什么，

sentences.en: but the sum total of all of them has really substantially reduced abortion access in the states that have practiced that strategy.
sentences.zh: 但所有这些法律的总和确实大大减少了实行这种策略的州的堕胎途径。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, in the same way,
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，同样地，

sentences.en: California has a pretty good reason to think that chipping away at access to guns will similarly curb guns in the state and gun deaths in the state.
sentences.zh: 加州有充分的理由认为，逐步侵蚀获取枪支的途径将同样遏制州内的枪支数量和涉枪死亡人数。

sentences.en: Because, as you've just described, that legal strategy has worked.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你刚刚所描述的那样，那种法律策略已经奏效了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I fully expect to cover more mass shootings in California.
sentences.zh: 我完全预计加州还会发生更多的大规模枪击事件。

sentences.en: I don't think it's going to end anytime soon.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这种情况很快就会结束。

sentences.en: But when you think about it this way, you know, it's not just chipping away at edges.
sentences.zh: 但当你从这个角度去思考时，你知道，这不仅仅是在边缘小打小闹。

sentences.en: This is not an abstract thing.
sentences.zh: 这不是一件抽象的事情。

sentences.en: The edges are people.
sentences.zh: 边缘指的是人。

sentences.en: There are people in the edges that are being chipped away at, you know.
sentences.zh: 边缘处有人正在被一点点剥离，你知道的。

sentences.en: So, it's lives.
sentences.zh: 所以，这关乎生命。

sentences.en: Sean, thank you.
sentences.zh: 肖恩，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: On Wednesday night, a man with a rifle and a handgun opened fire in a medical office building in Tulsa, Oklahoma, killing four people and then himself.
sentences.zh: 周三晚上，在俄克拉何马州塔尔萨市的一栋医疗办公楼里，一名手持步枪和手枪的男子开枪打死四人后自杀。

sentences.en: The police did not reveal the identity of the gunman, but said he was in his late 30s and that he had deliberately singled out the office building.
sentences.zh: 警方没有透露枪手的身份，但称他三十多岁，并且是有意挑中了这栋办公楼。

sentences.en: The Gun Violence Archive, a nonprofit that tracks gun deaths and defines mass shootings as four or more victims, counted it as the 233rd mass shooting so far this year.
sentences.zh: 追踪枪支暴力死亡人数并将群死群伤枪击事件定义为四名或更多受害者的非营利组织“枪支暴力档案”将其统计为今年迄今为止的第233起大规模枪击事件。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, the man accused of carrying out a racist shooting in Buffalo was charged with murder and with domestic terrorism.
sentences.zh: 周三，被控在布法罗制造种族主义枪击案的男子被控谋杀罪和国内恐怖主义罪。

sentences.en: The suspect, who is 18 and an avowed white supremacist, is accused of shooting 13 people, almost all of them black,
sentences.zh: 这名18岁的嫌疑人是一个公开宣称的白人至上主义者，他被控枪击了13人，其中几乎全部是黑人，

sentences.en: at a top supermarket in a largely black section of Buffalo on May 14th.
sentences.zh: 时间是5月14日，地点在布法罗一个黑人居多社区的一家顶级超市。

sentences.en: The domestic terrorism charge alleges that the suspect acted, quote, because of the perceived race of the people injured and killed.
sentences.zh: 国内恐怖主义罪名指控嫌疑人的作案动机是，引述，“由于受伤和遇难人员的假定种族”。

sentences.en: It carries a penalty of life imprisonment without parole.
sentences.zh: 该罪名可判处不得假释的终身监禁。

sentences.en: And a jury in Virginia awarded Johnny Depp $10 million in damages in the trial against his ex-wife, Amber Heard.
sentences.zh: 弗吉尼亚州的一个陪审团在约翰·德尼诉前妻安珀·赫德的官司中判决德普获得1000万美元的赔偿。

sentences.en: The jury found that Depp was defamed by Heard when she described herself, in a 2018 op-ed, as having been the victim of domestic abuse.
sentences.zh: 陪审团裁定，赫德在2018年的一篇专栏文章中将自己描述为家庭暴力的受害者时，对德普构成了诽谤。

sentences.en: Depp denied that, saying she had made up the claim.
sentences.zh: 德普对此予以否认，称她捏造了这一说法。

sentences.en: And the verdict, that capped a seven-week televised trial, seemed to vindicate him.
sentences.zh: 这场持续七周并通过电视转播的审判最终以这一裁决告终，似乎为他平反了。

sentences.en: However, the jury also found that Heard had been defamed, by one of Mr. Depp's lawyers.
sentences.zh: 然而，陪审团同时也裁定，赫德遭到了德普先生的一名律师的诽谤。

sentences.en: In a statement, Depp said the jury, quote, gave me my life back.
sentences.zh: 德普在一份声明中表示，陪审团引述，“把我的生活还给了我”。

sentences.en: Heard, in her own statement, said she was, quote, heartbroken by the verdict, and called it a setback for women.
sentences.zh: 赫德在自己的声明中表示，她对判决引述，“感到心碎”，并称这是一个对女性的打击。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Ricky Nowetsky, Rachel Quester, and Nina Feldman.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由里基·诺韦茨基、蕾切尔·奎斯特和妮娜·费尔德曼制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Liz O'Balen and Paige Cowett.
sentences.zh: 节目由莉兹·奥巴伦和佩奇·考维特剪辑。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Marianne Lozano and Dan Powell, and was engineered by Dan Powell.
sentences.zh: 包含玛丽安·洛扎诺和丹·鲍威尔的原创音乐，并由丹·鲍威尔担任混音工程。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由来自Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯伯格创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是本期《每日秀》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔韦尼西。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布法罗民主党一直像一个受严密控制的机器一样运转。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了许多自称是改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱有时又令人兴奋的权力争斗中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《都市》节目中，由我萨拉·凯尼格为您讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 都市。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在各大播客平台收听。

sentences.en: Let's see.
sentences.zh: 我看看。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。
